questions.q: A prescription has no doctor's signature or registration number. What should you do?
options: Give the medicine if the customer is a regular
Give only half the quantity
Hold it and tell the pharmacist it is not valid
Add the missing details yourself

questions.q: You cannot read one medicine name on a prescription. What is right?
options: Guess from the other medicines on it
Give the medicine the customer names
Check with the pharmacist, who can call the doctor
Give a common medicine with a similar name

questions.q: A prescription says 'Tab. X 1-0-1 for 5 days'. How many tablets is that?
Two strengths of one brand, 5 mg and 50 mg, sit side by side. How do you avoid a mix-up?
options: Match name and strength on the strip with the prescription
Pick by box colour, as you know the shelf
Ask the customer to check it at home
Take the one at the front of the shelf

questions.q: What does 'SOS' written next to a medicine on a prescription mean?
options: Take three times a day
Take before food only
Stop after one dose
Take only when needed

questions.q: A customer wants an antibiotic refilled on a prescription dated eight months ago. What do you do?
options: Refill it, as the doctor's name is on it
Refer to the pharmacist; a fresh prescription is usually needed
Give a smaller pack this time
Give a different antibiotic instead

questions.q: The prescribed strength is out of stock. You have another strength. The customer is in a hurry. What do you do?
options: Give the other strength and say adjust the count
Tell the pharmacist; a strength change needs the doctor's OK
Give the other strength without a word
Split tablets to match the dose

questions.q: A child's prescription shows an adult tablet strength. What is the safest step?
options: Dispense it, since the doctor wrote it
Tell the parent to give half a tablet
Stop and get the pharmacist to confirm with the doctor
Swap to a syrup of any strength

questions.q: A customer brings a prescription for two medicines. The pharmacy software shows an interaction warning between them. What do you do?
options: Ignore it, the doctor knows best
Remove one medicine from the bill
Tell the customer to take them on different days
Show the pharmacist before billing

questions.q: Where should unopened insulin vials be kept in the pharmacy?
options: On the shelf near the counter
In the fridge at 2–8 °C
In the freezer
In a dark drawer at room heat

questions.q: Which stock of a medicine should be sold first?
options: The newest batch received
Whatever is at the front of the shelf
The batch with the earliest expiry date
The batch with the higher MRP

questions.q: A strip's expiry date has already passed. What should you do with it?
options: Sell it at a discount
Move it to the expired stock area for return
Keep it on the shelf till month end
Give it free to a regular customer

questions.q: The medicine fridge reads 12 °C in the morning. What is the first thing to do?
options: Turn it to the coldest setting and say nothing
Move every item to the open shelf
Wait a day to see if it fixes itself
Report it and check the temperature log and stock inside

questions.q: Why should medicines be kept away from direct sunlight and damp places?
options: Heat and moisture can spoil them before expiry
Sunlight makes the labels hard to read
It matters only for syrups
Customers dislike faded boxes

questions.q: How should look-alike or sound-alike medicines be stored?
options: Together, so they are easy to find
In alphabetical order only
In the same box with a rubber band
Apart, with a clear shelf label or warning

questions.q: A new delivery arrives. The invoice says 20 boxes, but you count 18. What do you do?
options: Sign it as received and sort it out later
Add 2 boxes from old stock to match
Refuse the whole delivery
Note the shortage on the invoice and inform the supplier

questions.q: The system shows 30 strips of a Schedule H1 medicine, but the shelf has 26. What is right?
options: Report it at once and check the H1 register and bills
Change the system count to 26
Wait for next month's stock check
Order 4 more strips to cover it

questions.q: There was a long power cut overnight. The fridge with vaccines and insulin was off for many hours. What do you do?
options: Keep them aside, don't sell, and tell the pharmacist
Sell them, as they look fine
Put them in the freezer to cool fast
Sell them first at a discount

questions.q: A customer asks about side effects and you are not sure. What should you say?
options: Make a guess so they are not kept waiting
Let me ask the pharmacist for you
Tell them to search online
Say this medicine has no side effects

questions.q: When handing over medicines, what should you explain clearly?
options: Only the total bill amount
Which brand is cheaper online
When and how to take each one, as written
Your own advice on the dose

questions.q: An elderly customer can't read the small print on strips. What simple help can you give?
options: Tell them to ask a neighbour
Put all the tablets in one cover
Write the timing in large letters on each pack
Say it is written on the strip

questions.q: A customer asks for a strong painkiller without a prescription, saying their back hurts. What do you do?
options: Give a small strip just this once
Give it if they pay in cash
Explain it needs a prescription and call the pharmacist
Give a sleeping tablet instead

questions.q: A customer is angry that a medicine is out of stock. What is the best reply?
options: Tell them to try another shop
Give a different brand without asking anyone
Say it is the supplier's fault
Apologise, offer to order it, and give a time

questions.q: A customer wants to talk about a private health problem. What should you do?
options: Ask loudly so the pharmacist hears
Speak quietly and keep their details private
Tell them to come back when the shop is empty
Discuss it in front of others waiting

questions.q: A mother wants cough syrup for her 1-year-old without seeing a doctor. What do you do?
options: Advise her to see a doctor and call the pharmacist
Give an adult syrup and suggest a smaller dose
Give the syrup the child had last time
Sell the syrup most mothers buy

questions.q: A regular customer seems confused and says they took their BP tablets twice today. What do you do?
options: Tell them to skip tomorrow's dose
Give them water and send them home
Tell the pharmacist at once; they may need a doctor
Say it is fine, BP tablets are mild

questions.q: A customer wants to return a cut strip because the doctor changed the medicine. Shop policy does not take back cut strips. What do you do?
options: Take it back and put it on the shelf to resell
Politely explain the policy and ask the pharmacist
Argue until the customer leaves
Refund it without telling anyone

questions.q: Who must supervise the sale of prescription medicines in a pharmacy in India?
options: Any shop owner
A registered pharmacist
A medical representative
Any staff with two years' experience

questions.q: A strip is torn and its batch number and expiry are cut off. What should you do?
options: Sell it, the tablets are sealed
Write a date on it with a pen
Don't sell it; keep it aside
Sell it at a lower price

questions.q: What does the red vertical line on some medicine packs in India tell customers?
options: Use only on a doctor's prescription
It is an Ayurvedic medicine
It is safe for children
It is an imported medicine

questions.q: Why must you check the patient's name and age on a prescription before dispensing?
options: Only for the GST invoice
To make sure the medicine is for the right person
To offer a loyalty card
It is not needed for tablets

questions.q: A customer asks for a Schedule X medicine with an old photocopy of a prescription. What is right?
options: Do not sell; an original prescription is needed
Sell it, a copy is fine
Sell a smaller quantity
Sell it if they show an ID card

questions.q: How should the shop get rid of expired medicines?
options: Throw them in the shop's normal waste bin
Flush all of them down the drain
Send them back through the supplier's return system
Give them to a scrap dealer

questions.q: A person buys a codeine cough syrup every few days, each time with a different prescription. What do you do?
options: Inform the pharmacist; it may be misuse
Keep selling, the prescriptions are there
Sell only if paid in cash
Suggest a cheaper brand to them

questions.q: A drug inspector asks for the Schedule H1 register. What should it show for each sale?
options: Only the bill number
Only the customer's phone number
Patient and doctor name, medicine and quantity
Only the batch number

questions.q: A strip from a new supplier has spelling mistakes and odd printing. What do you do?
options: Sell it, as the price is low
Mix it with the old stock
Sell it only to new customers
Stop selling it and report it as a possible fake

questions.q: What is the most a customer can be charged for a medicine?
options: MRP plus GST
MRP plus a service charge
Any price the owner sets
The MRP on the pack

questions.q: A customer buys 4 tablets from a strip of 10 priced ₹50. What should the bill show?
A customer pays by UPI. When can you hand over the medicines?
options: As soon as they show their phone
After the payment shows as received
After they leave the counter
When a screenshot comes on WhatsApp

questions.q: A bill for a Schedule H medicine should show which details?
options: Patient name, doctor name, batch and expiry
Only the total amount
Only the customer's mobile number
The pharmacist's home address

questions.q: The MRP of a medicine is ₹112, including 12% GST. What is the price before GST?
At day end, the cash and UPI total is ₹350 less than the bills. What do you do first?
options: Put in ₹350 from your own pocket
Recheck bills, returns and UPI entries, then report
Delete one bill to match
Leave it for tomorrow's staff

questions.q: Why should the batch number be written on each bill?
options: It decides the GST rate
It is used to set the MRP
So the customer can claim a discount
So a recalled batch can be traced to buyers

questions.q: A company recalls one batch of a BP medicine. What should the pharmacy do?
options: Remove that batch, check bills and contact buyers if told to
Sell the remaining stock quickly
Remove all brands of BP medicine
Wait for customers to complain

task.title: Check a pharmacy bill and write a note to the pharmacist
task.brief: You are the pharmacy assistant. The bill below was made by a new staff member and is still with you. Take about 15 minutes. Write a short note to the pharmacist that lists every mistake you find in the bill, says why it matters, and says what should be done to fix it before the medicines are handed over. Use simple, clear points. A good note finds all the mistakes, puts patient safety first, and is polite.
task.material:
Ganga Medicals (sample shop), Hyderabad          Bill No. 1043      Date: 14-11-2026
Patient: Ravi K., 42 yrs      Doctor: (blank)

Item                              Batch    Expiry   Qty   MRP/unit   Amount
Cap. Amoxicillin 500 mg (Sch. H)  AM2231   08/2027   10    ₹9.50     ₹95.00
Cough syrup 100 ml                (blank)  10/2026    1   ₹85.00     ₹95.00
Tab. Paracetamol 650 mg           PC1190   03/2028   15    ₹2.00     ₹30.00
Cap. Omeprazole 20 mg             OM778    05/2028   10    ₹6.00     ₹60.00
                                         Total (incl. GST)          ₹290.00
Payment: UPI
key_points: Doctor's name is missing although the bill has a Schedule H antibiotic
Cough syrup batch number is missing
Cough syrup expired in 10/2026 and must not be sold; replace it from valid stock
Cough syrup is charged ₹95, above its ₹85 MRP
The correct total is ₹280 (or less once the syrup is fixed), not ₹290
Asks the pharmacist to check before handing over and corrects the UPI amount or refunds the difference

rubric.label: Mistakes found
rubric.guide: 0 = finds none or invents wrong ones, 3 = finds about half, 5 = finds all five mistakes correctly

rubric.label: Patient safety
rubric.guide: 0 = would let the expired or unverified item go out, 3 = mentions safety loosely, 5 = clearly stops the expired syrup and the incomplete prescription details

rubric.label: Fixes
rubric.guide: 0 = no fixes, 3 = some fixes, 5 = a clear fix for every mistake, including the total and payment

rubric.label: Clarity and tone
rubric.guide: 0 = confusing or rude, 3 = understandable, 5 = short, clear points in a polite, professional tone
